title: Greggs to shut four factories and cut 740 jobs
content_c:
Greggs to shut four factories and cut 740 jobs
- Published
High street bakery brand Greggs has announced plans to shut four of its factories and cut 740 jobs.
It plans to close manufacturing sites at North Lakes near Penrith, Cumbria, Pettigrews in Kelso, Scotland, Seaham in County Durham and Enfield, Greater London, though distribution operations would continue to run from the latter.
The proposals will also impact manufacturing operations at its Treforest site in Wales, but this will also continue as a distribution centre for the business.
The chain, which has headquarters in Newcastle, said its retail shops would not be affected by the proposed changes and like-for-like sales had grown across its managed stores.
It said the plans would save it about £20m across the 2028 and 2029 financial years.
The changes would take place over the next two and a half years, with parts of Greggs' manufacturing processes relocating, the firm said.
The range of products manufactured at its Clydesmill Glasgow and Manchester locations would be reduced and production of tinned bread at Gosforth would be stopped.
Some products would also be sourced from specialist suppliers.
The general secretary of the Bakers, Food and Allied Workers Union (BFAWU) Sarah Woolley said the union was "deeply concerned" about the announcement.
She said: "Our immediate priority is our members, their jobs, their families and the communities that could be affected by these proposals."
She added Greggs was clear in its own announcement the business continued to "perform strongly".
'No decisions made'
Greggs said positive trading and continued cost control means it expected a "modestly improved outcome" for 2026.
Like-for-like sales grew by 3.4% across its managed stores, with overall growth buoyed by the opening of new shops.
Woolley said Greggs' workers had played a "huge part" in getting the company where it is.
She said: "Against that backdrop, our members will understandably be asking why their jobs and livelihoods should now be put at risk in the name of efficiency and future progression."
But chief executive Roisin Currie said the company needed to "keep evolving alongside changing customer expectations".
She said: "Greggs manufacturing and logistics network remains a key strength of the business, and these proposals are intended to strengthen our manufacturing network, improve efficiency and ensure we remain well placed for the future while continuing to deliver the quality, value and service our customers expect."
The firm employs 33,000 people in the UK, the majority working in its stores.
A consultation with staff is expected to start soon and the company said "no final decisions" had been made yet.
'Sad day'
Kelso and district councillor Euan Robson said the announcement regarding Pettigrews in the Scottish Borders had come as a "bit of a shock".
He said: "Greggs is a very good business and apparently doing well, but it will be a sad day if the factory does close because it's been here for a very long time.
"It's been a very valued business in the local community; it employs quite a number of people, and thoughts today are really with them because it's an uncertain future."
The shake-up is expected to cost the firm about £60m, including disruption costs and redundancy payments.
The retail business said its sales grew by 7.7% in the three months to September 26, compared with the same period a year earlier.
It said this represented progress in the face of "challenging market conditions", as consumer finances continued to come under pressure.
The company said positive trading and continued cost control meant it expected a "modestly improved outcome" for 2026.
Greggs opened 95 new shops and closed 38 in the year to date, taking its overall estate to 2,796 shops.

title: MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities
content_c:
The security alert issued by MI5 regarding a Chinese state-owned conglomerate accused of conducting espionage in the UK reveals the extent to which British intelligence remains concerned about Beijing’s influence, and risks casting a shadow over UK-China cooperation at a time when the bilateral relationship is enjoying a revival.
The UK’s domestic security service on Wednesday warned researchers and academics to cease work with the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), an organisation MI5 described as a “significant threat”.
The CAGT, which is also known as the China General Technology Research Institute, is accused of paying UK academics working in sensitive fields such as artificial intelligence and cybersecurity for “research that directly improves MSS technical capability for espionage”. The MSS is China’s Ministry of State Security, its intelligence agency.
China’s approach to intelligence gathering involves hoovering up vast amounts of data, often from unsuspecting individuals who believe they are participating in normal research or consultancy work.
This year the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre warned businesses about Beijing-backed attempts to hack into everyday devices such as wifi routers.
Last year, MI5 issued another China-related security alert, warning parliamentarians about approaches from two LinkedIn profiles thought to be linked to Chinese intelligence.
Wednesday’s alert said academic institutions or researchers should be aware of the 2023 National Security Act, which makes it an offence to engage in conduct that is likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence agency. The warning is likely to send a chill through the UK’s cash-strapped higher education institutions, which have for years turned to China for funding and collaboration opportunities.
The UK is one of the leading countries to partner with China’s higher education sector. In May, China’s education ministry announced 219 new transnational education partnerships, with more than a fifth of the approvals being with British universities. That puts the UK at the top of the list of partner countries, ahead of Russia, France and Italy.
Chinese students are also the largest group of non-EU international students in the UK, generating about £600m a year for the higher education sector.
There has been growing concern in the UK that partnerships with China pose a risk to national security. The 2023 Intelligence and Security Committee report on China said UK academic institutions “provide a rich feeding ground for China to achieve both political influence and economic advantage” and flagged the risk of China “directing or stealing UK academic research”.
In this case, MI5 said that more than 100 academics linked to the UK had contributed to projects funded by the MSS via the front company. The areas of interest were AI, cybersecurity and steganography, the embedding of hidden data in pictures online.
Sam Goodman, the senior policy director at the China Strategic Risks Institute, said UK academics were “between a rock and a hard place” when trying to navigate areas of advanced interest that could be of interest to Chinese intelligence. “There is a lack of a coherent steer from government on something like AI. It isn’t particularly clear on AI at this juncture what levels of collaboration we can have with the Chinese,” Goodman said.
Analysts say the UK should do more to highlight which areas are of potentially dual-use interest to Chinese intelligence and provide more guidance to universities and academics.
“It’s all very well issuing these warnings,” says Charles Parton, a senior fellow at the Royal United Services Institute. “Actually far more important, surely, is a consideration of which technologies can be cooperated with China, and which can’t.” He said naming specific Chinese companies as a risk would not help UK researchers to do due diligence on every potential partnership. “The Chinese are not stupid. If they want to hide the origin of someone, they’ll do it,” Parton said.
Meia Nouwens, a senior fellow at the International Institute for Strategic Studies, said more clarity was needed on the UK side to help guide researchers working in sensitive fields.
Nouwens said: “A problem has been that in the past there hasn’t been a great deal of discussion of what areas of research constitute a national security risk. Without understanding the limits are of what the UK seeks to protect, it is impossible to have a conversation about managing risk.”
The MI5 alert specifically accused the CAGT of being a front for China’s intelligence. But any research institution in China is ultimately controlled by the Chinese Communist party. “Research institutes that are conducting research on areas of strategic interest for China such as technology will have oversight from the party-state,” Nouwens notes.
That does not mean any collaboration with Chinese educational institutions is inherently dangerous, but it does mean UK academics working in sensitive fields will feel increasingly uneasy about working with a country that has financially underpinned the UK’s higher education sector for decades.
author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent

title: Voters back Burnham’s plan to cut back triple lock to fund social care reform by 48% to 28%, poll suggests – as it happened
content_c:
Voters back Burnham's plan to cut back triple lock to fund social care reform by 48% to 28%, poll suggests
Sharon Graham, the Unite general secretary, said earlier this week that getting rid of the pensions triple lock to help fund social care reform would be “electoral suicide”.
This morning YouGov has published polling suggesting that she might be wrong. It suggests the voters support Burnham’s plan by 48% to 28%.
When people are asked in isolation if they support setting up a National Care Service, they were overwhelmingly in favour, by 74% to 11%.
YouGov also found that, when asked in isolation if they would back turning the triple lock into a double lock (by removing the earnings link), respondents were also in favour of that too, by 43% to 30%.
(In fact, Burnham’s proposal is more generous than a simply reversion to a double lock – see 8.45am.)
When YouGov put the two proposals together, and described them as Burnham’s plan, getting rid of the triple lock in its current form became more popular.
What people tell pollsters about a policy after it has just been announced may bear little resemblance to how they feel about it by the time it gets implemented. But these findings suggest Burnham is well placed to win the public argument on the merits of his policy.
When Rachel Reeves announced she was cutting the winter fuel payments in 2024, early polling showed that people opposed the move – and it was particularly unpopular with pensioners.
YouGov has published polling that suggests voters back Andy Burnham’s plan to make the pensions triple lock less generous to help fund the establishment of a National Care Service by 48% to 28%. (See 12.04pm.)
Angela Eagle, the environment secretary, has announced a £10m Good Food Neighbourhoods Programme. Explaining what it will do, Labour says:
The funding will be given to mayors and leaders in 45 local authorities to back community-led food projects like community food shops, mobile greengrocers, lunch clubs, community kitchens, and cooking and nutrition programmes.
Directed at areas facing some of the highest levels of deprivation and childhood obesity, each local authority will receive £222,000 to develop community-led solutions tailored to local needs.
The programme forms part of this Labour government’s promise of giving families room to breathe on the cost of living and communities the power to decide what works for them.
For a full list of all the stories covered on the blog today, do scroll through the list of key event headlines near the top of the blog.
In her conference speech, Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, also announced that the government is hiring more youth workers. She said:
Starting today, we are going to fund and recruit 1,000 youth workers, the biggest investment in youth work in a generation.
And we won’t stop there.
We will rebuild youth services, bring back youth work, and ensure every young person in this country, has someone who cares. No young person forgotten. No young person written off.
The Resolution Foundation thinktank has issued a statement this morning warmly welcoming the PM’s proposal to get rid of the pensions triple lock in its current form after the election.
The Institute for Fiscal Studies, another leading public spending thinktank, has also backed the PM’s proposal.
Nandy says for too long government has ceded too much power over internet to private sector
Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, criticised previous governments for giving private companies too much power over the internet revolution in her speech to the conference.
In the face of new technology, and in particular the threat that the internet posed to women, the state had been “far too small and far too timid for too long”, she said.
She went on:
I am on a mission to change it.
Because the World Wide Web – that created by Tim Berners Lee, to share knowledge, not exploitation - has revolutionised the way we live. An extraordinary democratic force, a source of connection, creativity and solace that has unleashed incomprehensible hatred, anger and polarisation - ask yourselves this, while it has undeniably shaped and defined us, have we done anything like enough to shape and define it?
Like the printing press, electricity and television, it has upended society. But what is almost unique to this moment is how absent the state - on behalf of its people - has been for so long. We have outsourced a revolution almost entirely to the private sphere to shape and police.
It is ... an almost violent indifference. To the women whose privacy and dignity is stripped from them. To the children who are preyed upon, their childhoods stolen. To people - how many of you in this room particularly women - hounded from public life. Where anger is monetised and profit put before people’s lives.
So conference, we are calling time on that indifference. Enough is enough.
Nandy said the government was introducing a social media ban for children and legislation to make it impossible for them to take or share nude images on their phones. She also said the government would take action to stop the circulation of non-consensual intimate images online.
Cooper says violence against women and girls public health problem as she announces £50m for support services
Yvette Cooper, the health secretary, also announced almost £50m to support victims of violence against women and girls. This should be seen as a public health problem, she said.
She told the conference:
We don’t treat violence against women and girls as the epidemic it really is. So here’s what we will change. For the first time, we will take a public health approach to violence against women and girls. We will work with survivors, charities, local government, and the NHS to set out how to treat this like the disease it is.
And today I am announcing the rollout of almost £50m support for new specialist referral services from GPs for women and men who are victims of domestic abuse.
Because conference when I stood here as home secretary two years ago and said our mission to halve violence against women and girls covered the whole of government, I meant it.
The money will ensure that victims of abuse can be referred to specialist help through GP practices under a new scheme called Steps to Safety. Around £34m will be spent allowing 12 integrated care boards to set up the programme, and £15m will go to victim support services in England.
Cooper is also appointing anational clinical lead for violence against women and girls to bring together clinical and public health expertise and strengthen the health system’s response.
Officials says health services are often the first places where victims of this sort of abuse disclose what has been happening.
Guess the tracks Burnham picked for each of England’s regions
At the Labour conference, Andy Burnham chose region-specific songs for the regional receptions he was attending. Alexis Petridis, the Guardian’s chief rock critic, has been assessing his choices. And he’s turned it into a quizz.
Brexit 'the biggest lie of the last 30 years', Macron says
Jakub Krupa
Jakub Krupa writes the Guardian’s Europe live blog.
Andy Burnham was critical of Brexit yesterday, but not as critical as the French president Emmanuel Macron who – not for the first time – has blasted those who campaigned for it.
Speaking with students at the Universidad Complutense de Madrid last night, Macron took aim at Brexit calling it “the biggest lie of the last 30 years.”
In a long defence of Europe’s unique integration process – where, according to Macron, even nationalist leaders have come to appreciate the bloc’s role – he described Brexit as a “disastrous exception” to the rule.
He said:
Brexit is the biggest lie of the last 30 years.
Those who said, ‘We’ll be richer,’ eight points of GDP less 10 years on. We’ll solve the immigration problem; it’s more complicated than before. And we’re going to be a huge success in international trade, it’s even worse.
Voters back Burnham's plan to cut back triple lock to fund social care reform by 48% to 28%, poll suggests
Sharon Graham, the Unite general secretary, said earlier this week that getting rid of the pensions triple lock to help fund social care reform would be “electoral suicide”.
This morning YouGov has published polling suggesting that she might be wrong. It suggests the voters support Burnham’s plan by 48% to 28%.
When people are asked in isolation if they support setting up a National Care Service, they were overwhelmingly in favour, by 74% to 11%.
YouGov also found that, when asked in isolation if they would back turning the triple lock into a double lock (by removing the earnings link), respondents were also in favour of that too, by 43% to 30%.
(In fact, Burnham’s proposal is more generous than a simply reversion to a double lock – see 8.45am.)
When YouGov put the two proposals together, and described them as Burnham’s plan, getting rid of the triple lock in its current form became more popular.
What people tell pollsters about a policy after it has just been announced may bear little resemblance to how they feel about it by the time it gets implemented. But these findings suggest Burnham is well placed to win the public argument on the merits of his policy.
When Rachel Reeves announced she was cutting the winter fuel payments in 2024, early polling showed that people opposed the move – and it was particularly unpopular with pensioners.
Cooper says government setting up collective pension scheme for workers in care sector
Yvette Cooper also announced that the government is setting up a new pension scheme for workers in the care sector in her speech to the Labour conference.
The health secretary said:
We will deliver the first-ever legally-binding fair pay agreement for care workers with minimum standards of pay and conditions across every employer, because care workers have been undervalued and underpaid for far too long.
We will publish a proper workforce plan for social care, proper career pathways, training, development of specialist skills.
We’ll offer thousands more academy places to help young jobseekers into good jobs in care, and thanks to the campaigning of all the Unison members in this hall, we will go further because it is just wrong that the people who work hardest to help others maintain dignity and respect in old age too often get nothing back from retirement themselves.
So, I can announce today we will introduce the first ever national collective pension scheme for workers in the care sector – fair pay, fair terms and conditions, and now a proper pensions scheme.
Cooper also said the government will appoint a new champion for unpaid carers to make sure the “voice of that hidden army is always heard in government”.
In an interview with Sky News, Kevin Hollinrake, the Tory chair, replied with a clear “no” when asked if his party would take part.
Hollinrake went on:
We think this is totally the wrong thing, despite the fact under any system of proportional representation, we’d have got more seats than we did in 2024, in that election.
That’s not the point. The point is you want decisive elections.
The public had a referendum on proportional representation back in 2011. It rejected it.
And we’re in an era now potentially moving into an era of sectarian politics, where you have small parties that represent particular interests, be it Gaza, be it Jeremy Corbyn’s Your Party.
Does anybody think it’d be a good idea for a government to be propped up by one of those parties who have single issue policies that really would be potentially very damaging to the UK itself and to our foreign relationships?
In fact, the referendum in 2011 was on the alternative vote – which is not strictly a proportional voting system, even though in UK politics it would deliver a more proportional outcome in some elections.
Yvette Cooper tells Labour conference 'Sure Start's back', as she expands healthy babies support programme
Yvette Cooper, the health secretary, has announced a Sure Start-style Healthy Babies programme for every local authority in England. Charlie Moloney the details here.
In her speech to the Labour conference, Cooper said:
Since the election, Bridget Phillipson and Lucy Powell have been working to rebuild family hubs across the country, bringing back support for parents and for young children.
But something is missing. In half of communities, compared to the last time round, the healthy babies services – mental health support for mums and dads, the feeding and bonding support for your new baby.
That changes now.
I can announce we will bring back the Sure Start health services into every family centre.
Reaching up to 1,000 hubs over the next two years.
One of the Labour party’s greatest achievements restored to families throughout the land.
So listen to that, George Osborne – Sure Start’s back.
That was a reference to an exchange Cooper had with George Osborne when she was interviewed by him over the summer for his podcast, Political Currency. As Tory chancellor, Osborne cut the funding for Sure Start, which Cooper helped to set up as a junior minister in the Blair government. Osborne now runs his podcast with Ed Balls, Cooper’s husband.
As the Tories ran down the Sure Start programme, Sure Start centres were replaced by family hubs. When Labour took power in 2024, these were beefed up as Best Start family hubs.
Sure Start is now widely regarded as one of New Labour’s most successful social programmes. A report by the Institute for Fiscal Studies said that it had a significant positive impact on the health and educational outcome of children. “For every £1 of net spending, Sure Start may eventually generate around £11 in benefits for the children who attended,” the IFS said.
Half a million trees to be planted in England in three years, environment secretary Angela Eagle says
Angela Eagle, the environment secretary, announced plans for half a million trees to be planted in England in the next three years to protect against extreme weather. Fiona Harvey has the details.
Eagle also announced plans for a Good Food Neighbourhoods Programme. She told the conference.
During our years in opposition, Britain became a poorer, more divided country. A country that seemed only to work for vested interests.
That’s why today, I’m announcing our Good Food Neighbourhoods Programme. Initially we’ll be supporting 45 communities - targeted at the areas with the highest levels of food inequality. Backed by £10m of investment, bringing fresh, affordable produce into neighbourhoods.
Creating community kitchens and supporting pensioners’ lunch clubs that tackle loneliness and hunger side by side. Because this is about more than what’s on someone’s plate. It’s about the ties that bind us together.
Tories accuse Burnham of going back on Makerfield byelection pledge to respect outcome of Brexit referendum
The Conservatives have accused Andy Burnham of going back on a byelection pledge not to consider rejoining the EU.
During the byelection in Makerfield, a constituency that strongly voted leave in 2016, Burnham said that the Brexit vote should be respected and that, if he was elected, he would not propose rejoining the EU.
But Burnham has now said this option should be considered. (See 7.49am.)
In response to Burnham’s Today interview, Alex Burghart said:
You cannot trust a word Andy Burnham says. Just a few weeks ago he said he wanted to move on from the Brexit arguments and now he is dragging Britain back into them by floating the prospect of rejoining the EU.
Labour cannot blame a democratic vote from over a decade ago for the consequences of their own economic decisions. While they look backwards, the Conservatives will look forwards.
Burnham says he has spent 'a lot of time' working out how to fill £4.7bn funding gap in defence investment plan
Andy Burnham has said that he has spent “a lot of time” working out how to fill the £4.7bn gap in the plans to fund the defence investment plan.
When Keir Starmer unveiled the defence investment plan in June, after he had announced he was standing down to make way for Burnham, he said the increased investment would cost £15bn. While explaining where most of the money would come from, he said the remaining funds – worth £4.7bn over four years – would have to come from savings to be announced in the budget.
In an interview on Times Radio, Burnham said that finding this money had been a “major priority”.
He said:
I said as soon as I came in that we would fully fund the defence investment plan. I’ve spent a lot of time on that and it will be fully funded.
There was a shortfall - there won’t be [at the budget].
author: Andrew Sparrow
description: This live blog is now closed‘Oozing everyman charm’: what the papers said about Burnham’s speechAndy Burnham has suggested that it would not be legitimate for a party to form a majority government with less than 30% of the vote.In his Today interview, asked why he wanted electoral reform and a move towards proportional representation, Burnham replied:I found it better being elected under a different system as mayor of Greater Manchester, where people had one or two, they could put that on the ballot paper.Because you had a reason to stop on every doorstep and chat to people who might not always support your party and try and get their second preference.No, it could happen with any political party. It’s whether that would be a legitimate government.I think you’ve got it completely wrong really, if you don’t mind me saying, to put it like that, because I have put out … a vision for a national care service.There are pensioners out there who watch your programme who are paying for care costs from their basic state pension. Now, is that right or fair? Continue reading...

title: Flydubai pilot investigated over possible attempt to crash Tel Aviv-bound flight
content_c:
Flydubai pilot stabbed in attempt to down Israel-bound plane
Published September 30, 2026last updated September 30, 2026
An Indian pilot was stabbed by his copilot on Wednesday in a failed attempt to crash a Flydubai plane that was bound for Israel.
After he was stabbed, Captain Smit Machchhar opened the cockpit in time for other passengers to intervene and the plane was ultimately able to land safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
Israel's defense minister, Israel Katz, said that "an attempted jihadist terror attack" had been thwarted after several passengers subdued the copilot.
Flydubai confirmed that all passengers were safe. It later announced it had suspended flights to and from Israel amid an ongoing investigation.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has now ordered authorities to "ramp up" security on both Israeli and non-Israeli carriers following the Flydubai flight incident.
Passengers return to Israel
On Wednesday evening, passengers from the diverted Flydubai flight arrived in Israel on a replacement plane, where numerous relatives were waiting for them.
Netanyahu also met with some of the passengers. A video posted to Netanyahu's X account showed him at the Tel Aviv airport meeting a man called Yaniv Hayoun who still had blood on his shirt after the midflight altercation.
The video described Yaniv as one of the passengers who entered the aircraft's cockpit.
Later, Netanyahu named the Indian pilot who was injured in an altercation with his co-pilot, who allegedly attempted to crash the Flydubai flight.
"My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery. Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster," Netanyahu wrote on social media.
"He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals."
The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said Machchhar is in stable condition and is being treated in a Tabuk hospital after an emergency landing.
 
Meanwhile, Israeli Foreign Minister said that he spoke with his UAE counterpart Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
"Mutual determination was expressed to strengthen relations between the countries on all levels and to collaborate against extremist elements seeking to harm security and undermine stability in the region," Saar wrote on X.
Saar also spoke with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul over the phone.
Wadephul said that he strongly condemned the incident as a serious attack on civil aviation. He added that his thoughts were with those who survived the flight and with those who feared for the lives of their loved ones. Wadephul also said that the circumstances surrounding the incident must be clarified quickly and thoroughly.
Later, US President Donald Trump announced he had discussed the Flydubai flight incident with Netanyahu. Trump said Netanyahu told him an Israeli plumber had helped prevent the aircraft from crashing.
"I did speak to Bibi Netanyahu at length about this event, and it seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack-job, and he stabbed the pilot," Trump told reporters.
What happened on the Flydubai flight?
Flydubai said flight FZ 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv experienced an "incident" while en route and landed safely in northwestern Saudi Arabia. The aircraft was a Boeing 737 MAX 8.
"The aircraft has landed safely in Tabuk Airport and all passengers are safe and accounted for," a Flydubai spokesperson said.
Later, a Flydubai spokesperson said that the reasons for an altercation that "occurred in the flight deck of flight FZ 1073" remained unknown and were under formal investigation.
"At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation. We urge all parties to refrain from premature speculation while authorities gather the facts," a spokesperson said in a statement published by the AFP news agency.
Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 initially showed a second Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, FZ1081, diverting back toward Dubai. It later showed the aircraft continuing toward Tel Aviv. There was no immediate explanation for the change.
How far did the plane fall?
The Israeli news portal Ynet reported that the aircraft entered a steep descent and that passengers helped one pilot prevent the other from crashing the plane.
Flight tracking data shows the aircraft suddenly losing around half its altitude as it neared Saudi Arabia's border with Jordan.
The plane dropped from nearly 34,000 feet (10,360 meters) at 05:21 GMT/UTC to below 17,000 feet (5,180 meters) at 05:22 GMT/UTC, according to Flightradar data.
Israel's Kan public broadcaster and Channel 12 reported that the Israeli military scrambled fighter jets amid initial fears of a possible hijacking. That possibility was later dismissed, according to the reports.
Israeli minister says 'attempted jihadist terror attack' thwarted
Israeli leaders announced that a "jihadist" pilot had attempted to crash a Flydubai plane carrying mostly Israeli passengers.
In a video message, Netanyahu said that "during the flight... one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot, and apparently tried to crash the plane with everyone on board."
He added that passengers and crew subdued the attacker, and the plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, where the pilot was arrested.
"I salute these heroes who showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage. They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster," Netanyahu said.
Meanwhile, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz described the incident as "an attempted jihadist terror attack" that was "thwarted only thanks to the heroism of several Israeli passengers."
Earlier, Netanyahu's office said he had held consultations over the incident and was monitoring developments.
"The incident is under control, and all measures are currently being deployed in order to return the Israeli passengers safely to Israel," his office said.
An unnamed senior Israeli government official told Channel 12 that a major disaster had been averted.
Meanwhile, Israel's Foreign Ministry informed its diplomats that the incident was "an attempted terrorist attack against Israelis, the United Arab Emirates, and the Abraham Accords."
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.
Edited by: Zac Crellin, Elizabeth Schumacher
description: A Flydubai service from the UAE to Israel made an emergency landing after the copilot stabbed the captain. Eyewitnesses said he attempted to crash the plane before he was subdued by passengers.

title: Burnham sieht starke Rolle Irans bei Vorfall nahe britischem Stützpunkt
content_c:
Vorfall nahe britischem Stützpunkt Burnham sieht "starke Hinweise" auf Rolle Irans
Großbritannien hat nach Angaben von Premier Burnham Hinweise, dass Iran in den Vorfall nahe dem Luftwaffenstützpunkt Fairford verwickelt ist. Teheran bestreitet jegliche Beteiligung. Viele Details sind weiter unklar.
Nach Angaben des britischen Premierministers Andy Burnham deutet einiges darauf hin, dass Iran an verdächtigen Aktivitäten an einem auch von den USA genutzten britischen Militärstützpunkt im Südwesten Englands beteiligt war.
Die Polizei hatte Samstagnacht fünf Männer festgenommen. Sie stehen im Verdacht, einen Anschlag geplant zu haben. Burnham machte keine näheren Angaben zu dem mutmaßlichen Vorhaben der Männer und erläuterte auch nicht, warum von einer Beteiligung Irans ausgegangen wird.
"Es gibt starke Hinweise darauf, dass Iran eine Rolle bei den Ereignissen gespielt hat, die sich an diesem Wochenende auf dem Stützpunkt der Royal Air Force in Fairford zugetragen haben", sagte der Labour-Politiker in einem Interview mit der BBC. Burnham verwies zugleich darauf, dass die Ermittlungen weiter liefen.
Iran hat jegliche Beteiligung an dem Vorfall zurückgewiesen.
Drei Lieferwagen und fünf Verdächtige
Die britische Polizei war in der Nacht zum Sonntag zu dem Stützpunkt der Royal Air Force gerufen worden, der auch von der US-Armee für den Krieg gegen Iran genutzt wird. Die Polizei entdeckte an dem Stützpunkt drei weiße Lieferwagen und nahm fünf Verdächtige fest.
Es handelt sich nach Polizeiangaben um britische Staatsbürger im Alter von 23 bis 25 Jahren, die alle in London wohnen. Die fünf Männer wurden schon am Montag vorläufig wieder auf freien Fuß gesetzt. Die Verdächtigen seien "nach umfangreichen Befragungen und Ermittlungen" unter Auflagen freigelassen worden, erklärte der Leiter der britischen Anti-Terror-Polizei, Laurence Taylor.
Viele Details zu dem Vorfall sind weiter unklar. Die britischen Behörden hatten sich bislang mit Äußerungen zu den möglichen Hintergründen stark zurückgehalten.
Trump kritisiert Freilassung auf Kaution
Die beschlagnahmten Fahrzeuge wurden nach Polizeiangaben umfassend untersucht. Spuren von Sprengstoff wurden nicht gefunden, teilte die Polizei am Dienstag mit. Allerdings sei Benzin gefunden worden.
Einer der Festgenommenen soll laut Medienberichten selbst den Notruf gewählt haben. Die Ermittler prüften den Berichten zufolge, ob der Mann einen Rückzieher gemacht habe oder ob der Anruf Teil des Plans gewesen sei.
US-Außenminister Marco Rubio hatte zuletzt bereits von einer Beteiligung eines "ausländischen Akteurs" gesprochen. Präsident Donald Trump hatte erklärt, die Männer hätten "großen Schaden" anrichten wollen. Der US-Präsident kritisiert zudem die Entscheidung der britischen Behörden, die Verdächtigen auf Kaution freizulassen.

title: So übt die Bundeswehr für den NATO-Verteidigungsfall
content_c:
So übt die Bundeswehr für den NATO-Verteidigungsfall
30. September 2026
Ein Hamburger Wohngebiet um Mitternacht, die Straßen sind still und leer. Plötzlich brandet Lärm auf: Mehrere Helikopter kreisen am Nachthimmel, Blaulicht erhellt die Dunkelheit. Eine lange Wagen-Kolonne rollt durch die Straßen. Auf gepanzerten Bundeswehr-Fahrzeugen stehen Soldaten mit Maschinengewehren im Anschlag. Für die Anwohner ein ungewohnter, vielleicht sogar beängstigender Anblick in der sonst so friedlichen Hafenstadt.
"Red Storm Charlie" heißt die Übung, die Teile der norddeutschen Hafenstadt drei Tage lang lahmlegt. Bundeswehr, Polizei und zivile Organisationen testen gemeinsam, wie gut sie auf den Ernstfall vorbereitet sind. Das Szenario: Eine verschärfte Bedrohungslage an der NATO-Ostflanke. Im Hamburger Hafen, dem größten Seehafen Deutschlands, landen NATO-Truppen - während der Übung dargestellt von Bundeswehr-Soldaten. Anschließend bewegen sie sich durch die Hansestadt in Richtung Osten. Sabotageakte und Demonstrationen, auch das ist Teil des Szenarios, behindern den Vormarsch. Mit rund 1700 Teilnehmenden, darunter 500 Soldatinnen und Soldaten, ist diese Übung (24.-26.09.2026) die bisher größte ihrer Art.
Eingebettet ist "Red Storm Charlie" in einen geheimen Plan: Den Operationsplan Deutschland. Mit diesem Dokument bereitet sich die Bundeswehr auf einen möglichen Angriff Russlands auf das NATO-Bündnisgebiet vor. Der Operationsplan Deutschland fügt sich nahtlos ein in die größeren Verteidigungsplanungen der NATO.
In einem Kriegs- oder Krisenszenario fiele nicht nur der Hafenstadt Hamburg, sondern ganz Deutschland eine besondere Rolle zu: die einer logistischen Drehscheibe für Hunderttausende NATO-Soldaten, Waffen und schweres Gerät. "Es handelt sich um einen sehr detaillierten und streng geheimen Plan, der festlegt, wo genau NATO-Verbündete in Deutschland anlanden müssten, insbesondere in welchen Häfen, und welche Routen für den Transit durch Deutschland erforderlich wären", erklärt Sicherheitsexpertin Aylin Matlé von der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Auswärtige Politik (DGAP) im DW-Interview.
Deutschland als Transitland für NATO-Truppen
Im Baltikum rechnet die NATO am ehesten mit einem Angriff Russlands. Dort würde sie im Ernstfall große Truppenkontingente aus ihren 32 Mitgliedsländern zusammenziehen. Soldatinnen und Soldaten aus Süd- und Westeuropa müssten dafür Deutschland passieren. "Konkret heißt das, dass innerhalb von sechs Monaten rund 800.000 Soldaten mit 200.000 Fahrzeugen durch unser Land ziehen müssten - das ist die Berechnung", erklärt Marcel Bohnert.
Der Bundeswehr-Offizier hat an der ersten Fassung des Operationsplans mitgearbeitet. Mit der DW spricht Bohnert als Privatperson, nicht als offizieller Vertreter der Bundeswehr. "Wir müssen garantieren, dass die Soldaten unsere Straßen und Häfen sicher nutzen können. Deshalb kümmern wir uns um alle ihre Bedürfnisse - um ihre Übernachtungsmöglichkeiten, um ihre Ernährung, wir sorgen für ihre Sicherheit, wir führen sie durch unser Straßennetz."
Auch für Transporte in die Gegenrichtung, also von Osten nach Westen, trifft der Plan Vorkehrungen, etwa für die Passage von verwundeten Soldaten oder flüchtenden Zivilisten. Den Auftrag, den Plan zu entwickeln, erteilte Bundeswehr-Generalinspekteur Carsten Breuer nach dem Großangriff Russlands auf die Ukraine 2022. Breuer ist der ranghöchste deutsche Soldat, und nicht nur ihn treibt die Sorge um, dass Russland weitere Länder angreifen könnte. Schon jetzt sieht sich Deutschland einer Vielzahl russischer Provokationen ausgesetzt - von Cyberangriffen bis hin zu Sabotageakten gegen die Bundeswehr.
Verteidigungsminister Pistorius: "Moskau testet unsere Reaktion"
Eine neue Dimension der Bedrohung stellte der Anschlagsversuch Anfang August am Flughafen Leipzig/Halle dar. Dort kam eine mit Sprengstoff präparierte Drohne zum Einsatz, die nur dank glücklicher Umstände nicht explodierte. Die Bundesregierung macht Russland dafür verantwortlich. "Die Bedrohung wird konkreter. Sie ist ernst, sie ist akut, und sie wird immer sichtbarer. Das ist genau das, was der russische Präsident will. Moskau testet unsere Reaktion", sagte Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius (SPD) am 23. September im Bundestag.
Dieser Bedrohung tritt die Bundeswehr auch mit dem Operationsplan Deutschland entgegen, der stetig weiterentwickelt wird. Erkenntnisse aus Übungen wie "Red Storm Charlie" fließen mit ein. Der Plan diene auch der Abschreckung, sagt Marcel Bohnert: "Wir hoffen, dass wir Russland von seiner Aggression abhalten können, indem wir unsere Stärke demonstrieren - durch den raschen Ausbau unseres Militärs sowie die sehr organisierte und schnelle Verlegung von Streitkräften an die Grenzen."
Straßen und Brücken müssen auf Vordermann gebracht werden
Wie gut ist Deutschland vorbereitet auf seine Rolle als militärische Drehscheibe? Einen Schwachpunkt sieht Sicherheitsexpertin Aylin Matlé in der teils maroden Infrastruktur. Insbesondere müsse Deutschland sich "viel schneller und gründlicher" um die Instandhaltung und Reparatur von Brücken, Straßen und Verkehrswegen kümmern, über die die Truppentransporte laufen sollen. "Denn einige dieser Anlagen stammen noch aus der Zeit des Kalten Krieges und sind nicht für den Transport schwerer Lasten oder Ausrüstung ausgelegt."
Eine weitere Schwierigkeit: Die Balance zwischen der Geheimhaltung des Plans und der Einbindung der Öffentlichkeit. Aus Furcht vor Sabotageakten sollen sensible Informationen, etwa die genauen Transitrouten für die NATO-Truppen, nicht in die Hände Russlands fallen. Andererseits funktioniert der Plan nur im Zusammenspiel der Bundeswehr mit der Zivilgesellschaft - mit den Verantwortlichen in Städten und Gemeinden, mit der Polizei und Hilfsorganisationen. "Teile des Plans müssen öffentlich zugänglich sein, da wir die Gesellschaft sowie Ministerien und Regierungen dafür brauchen", sagt Marcel Bohnert.
Könnte die AfD sensible Informationen weitergeben?
Die Diskussion über die Geheimhaltung des mehr als 1000 Seiten umfassenden Dokuments flammte jüngst wieder auf, nachdem die Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) aus der Wahl im ostdeutschen Bundesland Sachsen-Anhalt als stärkste Partei hervorging. Sicherheitsexperten äußerten die Sorge, dass die in Teilen rechtsextreme und Russland-freundliche Partei Informationen aus dem Plan nach Moskau weitergeben könnte, sollte sie den Ministerpräsidenten stellen. Aus dem Verteidigungsministerium heißt es dazu: Kein Bundesland erhalte das vollständige Dokument. Vielmehr würden die sensiblen Teile des Operationsplans nur in Ausschnitten und sehr gezielt weitergegeben.
Beobachtern zufolge verstärkt die wachsende Zahl hybrider Bedrohungen dennoch das Bedürfnis nach Geheimhaltung. Bei der Übung "Red Storm Charlie" in Hamburg wurden die akkreditierten Reporter über Routen und Schauplätze bis zuletzt im Unklaren gelassen - aus Sorge vor Störungen und möglicher Sabotage.
description: Wie verteidigungsbereit ist die Bundesrepublik? Der Operationsplan Deutschland gibt Antworten. Militär-Übungen wie "Red Storm Charlie" stellen sie auf die Probe.

title: Gletscherschmelze: Schweiz verzeichnet zweitstärksten Gletscherschwund seit Messbeginn
content_c:
Die diesjährige Hitzewelle in Europa und der schneearme Winter haben den Gletschern in der Schweiz laut einer Studie zugesetzt. Die Gletscher in der Alpenrepublik verloren in diesem Jahr 5,5 Prozent ihrer Masse, wie das Schweizerische Gletschermessnetz Glamos mitteilte. Damit verzeichnete dieses Jahr den zweitstärksten Gletscherschwund seit Beginn der Aufzeichnungen vor rund 140 Jahren.
Laut dem Bericht war die schützende Schneedecke auf den Gletschern in diesem Jahr bereits während der Hitzewellen im Juni teilweise verschwunden. Bis September war sie demnach selbst in großen Höhen komplett weggeschmolzen. Juni, Juli und August waren nach Angaben des Schweizer Wetterdienstes die heißesten in der Schweiz seit Beginn der Aufzeichnungen 1864.
Das Volumen der Gletscher in den Alpen geht seit mehr als einem Jahrhundert zurück. In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten beschleunigte sich diese Entwicklung aufgrund der vom Menschen verursachten Erderwärmung. Binnen fünf Jahren verloren die Gletscher dem Bericht zufolge fast ein Fünftel ihrer Masse.
Schweiz hat bessere Ausgangslage als Österreich
Besonders sichtbar wurde der Rückgang laut dem Institut am Gletscher Scex Rouge. Dieser wird laut Glamos-Leiter Matthias Huss nicht überleben. »In zehn oder vielleicht fünfzehn Jahren wird es wahrscheinlich kein Eis mehr geben«, sagte Huss. Er sprach gegenüber der Nachrichtenagentur AFP von einem »katastrophalen Jahr« für die Gletscher.
In der Schweiz, wo fast 50 Gipfel auf einer Höhe von über 4.000 Metern liegen, haben die Gletscher zwar bessere Chancen als in Österreich, die immer heißeren Sommer zu überstehen. Dennoch teilte Glamos mit: »Alpengletscher haben unter solchen Bedingungen langfristig keine Überlebenschance.«
Insgesamt hat die Schweiz rund 1.400 Gletscher, von denen das Messnetz regelmäßig 23 vermisst und danach Hochrechnungen macht.
author: DIE ZEIT: Umwelt - Simon Sales Prado
description: Gletscher in der Schweiz haben in diesem Jahr rund fünf Prozent ihrer Eismassen verloren. Die Schneedecke war wegen der Hitze teils bereits im Juni geschmolzen.

title: Економіка Росії на межі "великої кризи" – розвідка Данії
content_c:
Економіка Росії на межі "великої кризи" – розвідка Данії
Економіка Росії перебуває на межі "великої кризи" через військові витрати, міжнародні санкції та українські удари по російській енергетичній інфраструктурі.
Про це пише Axios із посиланням на оцінку Данської служби оборонної розвідки.
"Водночас російська економіка перебуває на межі великої кризи, спричиненої військовими витратами, міжнародними санкціями та українськими ударами по російській енергетичній інфраструктурі", — йдеться в документі.
На цьому тлі датська розвідка очікує посилення гібридних атак Росії проти Заходу та НАТО. Йдеться, зокрема, про руйнівні кібератаки та диверсії проти підприємств і транспортних маршрутів, що забезпечують допомогу Україні.
Читайте також: Ще два роки війни. Економіка Росії відмовляється впадати в рецесію
Нагадаємо:
Росії загрожує "вибухова" банківська криза, оскільки фінансові установи беруть на себе значну частину тягаря військової економіки країни, йдеться у звіті розвідки ЄС.
Рекордні 60% росіян, опитаних у період з березня по травень, зазначили, що економічна ситуація в регіонах погіршується, поліпшення бачать 27% респондентів.
author: Економічна правда

title: У Києві внаслідок російської атаки загорілися кафе та склад
content_c:
У Києві внаслідок російської атаки загорілися кафе та склад
Росія продовжує атаки на Київ дронами та ракетами (Фото: REUTERS/Gleb Garanich)
Увечері 30 вересня російські війська знову атакували Київ. У Солом’янському районі внаслідок удару виникла пожежа в кафе. Атака продовжилася вночі 1 жовтня.
02:52 Жовтий рівень небезпеки в Києві через загрозу дрону.
Про це повідомили у Київській міській військовій адміністрації.
В Оболонському районі столиці загорілася складська будівля. Ще на одній локації в цьому районі уламки впали на відкритій території.
Інформація про можливих постраждалих та інші наслідки атаки уточнюється.
У ніч проти 30 вересня Росія атакувала Київ балістичними ракетами та безпілотниками. Влучання, падіння уламків і пошкодження фіксували у низці районів столиці. Внаслідок ударів загинули люди, були поранені.

content_c:

У Солом’янському та Оболонському районах Києва внаслідок ворожої атаки виникли пожежі, ще на одній локації зафіксували падіння уламків.

Про це повідомили у Київській міській військовій адміністрації.
У Солом’янському районі внаслідок атаки загорілося кафе, розташоване на першому поверсі житлового будинку.
В Оболонському районі виникла пожежа у складській будівлі.
Крім того, ще на одній локації в Оболонському районі уламки впали на відкритій території.
Інформацію про можливих постраждалих та масштаби пошкоджень наразі уточнюють.
Нагадаємо, що Одеса під ударом РФ: пошкоджено інфраструктуру, наслідки уточнюють

title: День защитников и защитниц Украины: поздравления и открытки
content_c:
1 октября в Украине отмечают День защитников и защитниц Украины. В этот день поздравляют военных, которые защищают нашу страну от врага. Издание CHAS.NEWS собрало поздравления к празднику.
Поздравления ко Дню защитников и защитниц Украины
Поздравляю с Днём защитников и защитниц Украины! Спасибо за силу, смелость и ежедневный труд ради нашего государства. Желаю выдержки, надёжных людей рядом, крепкого здоровья и скорейшего возвращения домой к тем, кто любит и ждёт.
***
Искренне поздравляю с 1 октября! Пусть хватает сил преодолевать все испытания, рядом всегда будет надежное плечо, а каждый день приближает победу и мирное будущее Украины. Берегите себя!
***
С Днём защитников и защитниц Украины! Низкий поклон за мужество, стойкость и преданность. Желаю безопасности, здоровья, выдержки и тепла родного дома. Пусть любовь близких поддерживает даже на самом большом расстоянии.
***
Спасибо за возможность жить, работать, учиться и обнимать родных в своей стране. Желаю сил, хороших новостей, надёжной защиты и людей, которым можно доверять. Пусть каждая дорога ведёт домой.
***
В День защитников и защитниц Украины желаю выдержки, внутреннего равновесия и веры в собственные силы. Пусть опасность обходит стороной, побратимы и сестры поддерживают, а дома всегда ждут с любовью.
***
Поздравляю с праздником и искренне благодарю за службу Украине. Желаю крепкого здоровья, стойкости, удачных решений и спокойствия для родных. Пусть впереди будет как можно больше светлых дней и счастливых встреч.
***
С Днём защитников и защитниц! Ваша отвага и стойкость вызывают безграничную благодарность. Пусть силы восстанавливаются, надежда не угасает, а поддержка миллионов украинцев придаёт уверенности каждый день.
***
Примите самые искренние слова уважения и благодарности. Желаю безопасности, крепкого здоровья, выдержки и добрых людей рядом. Пусть Украина бережет каждого и каждую, кто её защищает.

title: Як обрати подушку, щоб добре спати і не боліла шия: поради експерта
content_c:
Як обрати подушку, щоб добре спати і не боліла шия: поради експерта
  - Author, Джордж Сандеман
  - Role, ВВС
- Published
- Час прочитання: 5 хв
Подушка може бути м'якою, дорогою і навіть ортопедичною - але це не означає, що вона вам підходить. Важливо також, як ви спите, ширина ваших плечей і жорсткість матраца.
"Я з тих людей, які беруть подушку з собою", - зізнається доктор Маккарті.
Можливо, ви бачили таких людей в аеропорту: в одній руці валіза, під пахвою - подушка.
А може, ви й самі з таких. Бо коли нарешті знаходиш подушку, на якій добре спиться, міняти її на першу-ліпшу готельну вже не хочеться.
І це не просто забаганка. Невдала подушка справді може стати причиною болю в шиї.
Маккарті - фізіотерапевт і доцент Манчестерської школи фізіотерапії. Він пояснює, на що звернути увагу, коли обираєте подушку, і як навіть звичайну готельну зробити зручнішою.
У якій позі ви спите?
За словами Маккарті, насамперед треба врахувати, в якій позі ви зазвичай спите.
У подкасті BBC він умовно поділяє людей на три групи:
- тих, хто спить на боці,
- на спині
- і на животі.
З тими, хто спить на животі, все просто: Маккарті просто цього не радить.
У такому положенні шия годинами повернута в один бік.
"Якийсь м'яз чи зв'язка неминуче перенапружуються і можуть боліти, - каже він. - Якщо у фізіотерапії й існує загальноприйнята думка щодо лікування болю в хребті, то це порада не спати на животі".
Тим, хто спить на спині, варто звернути увагу на вигин верхньої частини хребта. З віком у багатьох людей він стає помітнішим.
"Якщо вигин у вас сильніший, вам потрібна трохи вища подушка, ніж людині з дуже прямою спиною", - пояснює експерт.
А якщо ви спите на боці, головне - ширина плечей. Загальне правило таке: що ширші плечі, то вищою має бути подушка.
Але це ще не все. Є ще одна важлива річ - ваш матрац.
Жорсткий чи м'який матрац?
На перший погляд здається, що матрац тут ні до чого. Насправді ж він дуже впливає.
За словами Маккарті, важливо, наскільки сильно тіло занурюється в матрац.
"Якщо у вас широкі плечі й дуже жорсткий матрац, вам потрібна висока подушка, - пояснює він. - А якщо матрац м'який, подушка має бути тоншою, тому що плече сильніше занурюється в матрац".
Для тих, хто спить на спині, це не так важливо. У такому положенні тіло занурюється в матрац значно менше, ніж коли людина лежить на боці.
Якщо подушка здається вам надто низькою, спочатку спробуйте простий трюк: покладіть під неї складений рушник.
Підгортайте або розгортайте його, щоб підібрати потрібну висоту подушки.
Коли влаштує - приблизно виміряйте її. Цей розмір допоможе вам зорієнтуватися, коли купуватимете нову.
Чи справді потрібна анатомічна подушка?
На полицях магазинів можна знайти безліч спеціальних моделей - анатомічних, ергономічних, ортопедичних. Виробники обіцяють правильну підтримку голови й шиї.
Але, за словами Маккарті, переконливих наукових доказів їхньої переваги поки немає.
"Є невелика кількість досить слабких доказів того, що трохи вища передня частина подушки, яка підтримує шию... справді допомагає [тим, хто спить на боці]".
Зрозуміти, чи потрібна вам така форма, можна знову ж таки за допомогою рушника.
Скрутіть його й покладіть під подушку - так, щоб трохи підняти її в зоні шиї.
Якщо ви спите на боці, стежте за головним: спина має залишатися прямою.
Для тих, хто спить на спині, деякі виробники роблять подушки із заглибленням посередині та вищими краями. За словами Маккарті, така форма справді допомагає утримувати голову й шию у правильному положенні.
Щоправда, подобається вона не всім. Деяким його пацієнтам такі подушки здаються "трохи клаустрофобними".
Є ще один нюанс. Якщо у вас велика й важка голова, каже Маккарті, вам потрібна вища та щільніша подушка.
Пух, перо чи піна?
Тепер - про наповнювач.
Пухові та пір'яні подушки добре пропускають повітря й допомагають регулювати тепло: вони не дають голові перегріватися, але водночас добре зберігають тепло, коли це потрібно, каже Маккарті.
Але є проблема: за ніч така подушка може втратити форму.
Особливо, якщо ви крутитесь уві сні. Наповнювач поступово зміщується до узголів'я, і подушка вже не підтримує голову так, як на початку ночі.
"Те, що спочатку було приємною, рівною поверхнею, яка добре підтримувала голову, перетворюється на клин, і шия опиняється в неприродно зігнутому положенні".
Подушки з холофайбером або мікрофіброю краще тримають форму. Щоправда, тепло вони зазвичай відводять гірше.
Є моделі, у яких нижня частина зроблена з щільнішого матеріалу. Завдяки цьому подушка краще тримає форму протягом усієї ночі.
Сам Маккарті користується подушкою з піни з каналами всередині. Вони допомагають повітрю вільно циркулювати й не дають подушці перегріватися.
Оскільки спить на боці, висоту подушки він регулює за допомогою складеного рушника, який кладе під неї.
Ідеальної подушки не існує
Головний висновок Маккарті такий: подушку доводиться підбирати під себе.
Те, що зручно одній людині, іншій може зовсім не підійти.
Тому фізіотерапевт радить, якщо є така можливість, користуватися пробним періодом, який деякі виробники дають покупцям.
"Не існує єдиної конструкції, яка ідеально підходила б усім і для будь-якої пози під час сну, - каже він. - Подушку справді доводиться підбирати індивідуально".
Тож наступного разу, коли ви прокинетеся з болем у шиї, варто звернути увагу не лише на те, як ви спали.
description: Ваша подушка може бути причиною болю в шиї - навіть якщо вам здається, що спати на ній зручно.

title: У Харкові ворожий дрон влучив у житлову багатоповерхівку та ТЦ: одна людина поранена – Терехов
content_c:
Російські окупаційні війська атакували Харків бойовими безпілотниками, зафіксовано влучання в Київському районі міста, зокрема в торговельний центр та житлову багатоповерхівку, відомо про одну поранену людину, повідомив міський голова Ігор Терехов у телеграм-каналі.
"Зафіксовано влучання ворожого безпілотника у Київському районі. Наслідки уточнюються", – спершу написав мер.
Згодом він додав: "Ворог ударив бойовим дроном по одному з торгівельних центрів... Надійшла інформація про одну поранену людину".
Пізніше Терехов уточнив дані щодо наслідків удару: "За уточненою інформацією, зафіксовано влучання у багатоповерховий житловий будинок".
На місцях прильотів працюють відповідні екстрені та комунальні служби, інформація щодо постраждалих і руйнувань продовжує оновлюватися.

title: Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster
content_c:
Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster
- Published
Six people traffickers have been found guilty in France of causing the deaths of 31 migrants in the worst ever small-boat accident in the Channel.
At the end of a four-week trial in Paris, the six were convicted of "involuntary homicide" and given prison terms of between six and 10 years.
Seven others were given lesser sentences of up to four years, and one person was found not guilty.
The boat went down early in the morning on 24 November 2021 after sending distress calls to French and British coastguards. The dead, including a child of seven, were mainly Iraqi Kurds but also included Afghans, Egyptians and Iranian Kurds. Only two men survived.
The charge sheet said the migrants had been put to sea from the French coast in a boat "that was of poor quality, uncertified, unsuitable for navigation at sea, overloaded, and without correct life jackets".
The trial established that the guilty men were members of two separate networks – one of which was Iraqi Kurd, the other Afghan – that co-operated to organise the cross-channel journey and bring migrants to the meeting point.
Unusually the court was attended at the start by several family members, who came to France from Iraqi Kurdistan and gave moving testimony about how the victims came to be on board the boat.
Speaking after the verdict, their lawyer Matthieu Chirez said the decision "comes as a relief for all the civil plaintiffs because it confirms the penal responsibility of the traffickers". He said the trial had "humanised the families of victims".
One family member, Zana Marmand Muhammed, told the court how his younger brother Twana had "wanted to go to England to find a job and because the geopolitical situation with us is dangerous. No-one in the family wanted him to leave, but we could not dissuade him."
Nabi Mustafa Mina, the father of Zanyar who was 19 when he died, told of how he tried to dissuade his son from leaving.
"I said I would help him to get married, I would give him my house, I would divide my salary in two. But no, he said he wanted a better life, that he would get by somehow. I ran out of arguments," he said.
The family-members explained how they had paid a deposit at a bank in Iraqi Kurdistan and then followed their loved ones' progress through Turkey, Italy and then France. In one of the last messages from Twana, he posted a picture of himself at the Eiffel Tower.
The court also heard a statement from one of the two survivors, Issa Omar, read out by his lawyer. Omar said that he "would have liked to appear before the judge but I do not have the strength. Since the wreck I have the impression that part of me disappeared beneath the waves."
His lawyer Matthieu Chirez said that Omar had "clung to floating bodies, to a life-jacket. He survived by keeping his eyes open so as not to go to sleep, and swimming to keep his heart beating".
Police investigating the disaster used phone tracking to identify members of the two networks.
The lesser figures were accused of sheltering migrants, transporting them across France to the so-called "jungle" camp outside Calais, and helping on the night of the departure.
The alleged leader of the Iraqi Kurd network – named as Bashdar – was not a defendant in the trial. He is in custody in Iraq. His close aide – Harem Ahmed Abawaker – was given eight years in prison.
The biggest sentence, of 10 years, went to Obaidullah Maroofkhel, who ran the Afghan network. He was tried in his absence along with one other defendant.
Most of the 14 were Afghans or Iraqi Kurds. All but one of the defendants appeared in the trial as free men, so following the verdict the court issued six arrest warrants.
A separate police investigation is under way into seven members of the French armed forces for allegedly failing to come to the help of the migrants on the night of the disaster.
The seven were at the regional sea rescue centre or on board a navy ship, and are alleged to have ignored distress calls from the boat. A decision on whether to recommend them for trial will be taken in the coming months.
The trial ended as France and the UK announced it was ending the so-called one-in one-out scheme under which the British government sent back irregular cross-Channel migrants to France, and in return accepted individuals with a likely prospect of being granted asylum.
France had already signalled that the year-long programme, which has seen a little more than 1,000 migrants switch country, was not producing expected results in breaking the traffickers' business model.

title: UK-France 'one in, one out' migrant scheme scrapped
content_c:
UK-France 'one in, one out' migrant scheme scrapped
- Published
The UK government has announced the "one in, one out" agreement with France to send back some migrants who cross the Channel has been scrapped.
The pilot scheme allowed the UK to return some small boat arrivals while agreeing to take in the same number of people from France who were believed to have a legitimate claim to come to Britain.
Only around 1,500 people have been removed to France since the scheme began just over a year ago.
The BBC understands the government would have liked the scheme to continue, but felt it did not reach the desired scale.
A Home Office spokesperson said "lessons learned" would be used to "accelerate efforts" to return small boat migrants with no right to remain.
"The government's pilot with France to remove asylum seekers in exchange for an equal number of legal migrants is no longer processing new cases," the spokesperson said.
"However, flights will continue over the coming weeks to swiftly remove small boat migrants from the UK, and we will use lessons learned from the pilot to accelerate efforts to return small boat migrants with no right to remain in the UK."
The government would continue working with France to tackle small boat crossings, the spokesperson said, adding that "real progress" had been made with numbers "significantly down on last year".
The French Interior Ministry told the BBC: "We are discussing with the British the terms of exit from the agreement."
Earlier this month, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood admitted the scheme had "not been without its challenges".
"The numbers are still relatively small," she told MPs.
"What has been more operationally difficult is to scale up very large numbers of removals every week into the French system."
However, she also said the UN and other agencies had reported that some migrants were not getting on small boats because they thought there was a chance they could be accepted under the "one in, one out" scheme.
So far this year, 19,135 people have made the Channel crossing, which is 42% lower than the same period in 2025 when 32,188 crossed in small boats.

title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest
content_c:
The AI telling farmers when to harvest
- Published
When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
"It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits. "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning."
He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful. "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe. How long do you have to pick it?" he says. "That's where these models are really helpful."
Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example. The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity. Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
But planning a harvest is tricky. New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging. It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly. Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines. The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by. AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
"Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter. He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter. "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains. "It's going to be bespoke to your farm."
Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter. For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
"If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes. "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask? Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas. "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't."
The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK. This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts. The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate). We guarantee less than 20% error…"
Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast. AI tech for forecasting fruit ripeness is not yet "a finished solution" says operations director Neill Finlayson: "This journey is still ongoing and, whilst significant progress has been made, the industry remains some way from achieving a fully integrated forecasting ecosystem."
Driscoll's, a California headquartered fruit seller with a big operation in the UK, also confirmed to BBC News that some of its independent fruit growers in the UK have used FruitCast's technology.
Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail. Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop. These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements. But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.
She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector, external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops. Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey. "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.
Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.
But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile. "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University. "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works."
Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries, external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.
The simplest systems need not be expensive. Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery, external from $100 (£74) drones.
In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions. However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.
Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US. He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".
But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence. "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.
